clue.text: Right outfit's pretentious on barman in theatre

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece placed on another follows it
the barman is placed inside the word for theatre

parts.note: rep is short for repertory theatre
a publican runs a pub and serves behind its bar
arty describes someone affectedly artistic

explanation.surface: A snooty drinks-server is being cast in a stage production.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outfit' reads as clothing; here it means an organisation.
explanation.definitionFit: The Republican Party is the main right-wing political organisation in the US, an outfit being a group or team.

clue.text: Hacks through grass that's kept down

indicators.note: one word is driven through the middle of the other, so it sits inside

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass of wetlands
hacks are journalists, collectively the press

explanation.surface: Someone cutting their way through overgrown grass that has been trodden flat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hacks' looks like a verb of chopping; it is a noun for reporters.
explanation.definitionFit: Repressed means held back or suppressed, the same as kept down.

clue.text: Person who's paid before international rally?

indicators.note: the first piece comes before the second in a down answer

parts.note: a pro, short for professional, is paid to play
a test is an international match in cricket or rugby

explanation.surface: A paid sportsperson warming up before an international fixture.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'rally' is not a tennis exchange but a demonstration.
explanation.definitionFit: A rally can be a mass demonstration, which is a kind of public objection or march.

clue.text: Man who's learned caution: leader of mob holding bank up

parts.note: to book someone is to caution them officially, as police or referees do

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from bottom to top
the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: a bank of seats or switches is a row

explanation.surface: A cautious man keeps a gang boss's money in a vault.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bank' suggests money; it is a row, as in a bank of seats. To book someone is to caution them, as a football referee does.
explanation.definitionFit: A bookworm is a keen reader, someone devoted to learning from books.

clue.text: Primate of country in Asia nearly crossing river

indicators.note: the river letter is set across the shortened country, so inside it
nearly means the last letter of the country is dropped

parts.note: India is a large country in South Asia
R is the standard abbreviation for river on maps

explanation.surface: A monkey from somewhere in Asia wades almost across a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly' drops the last letter of INDIA to leave INDI, and 'crossing' puts R inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The indri is a large lemur of Madagascar, and lemurs are primates.

clue.text: Offensive broadcast to stop working

parts.note: to air a programme is to broadcast it
to strike is to stop work in protest

explanation.surface: A rude programme is aired, prompting staff to walk out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Offensive' reads as an adjective meaning rude; it is a noun for a military attack.
explanation.definitionFit: An air strike is an attack from aircraft, so a military offensive.

clue.text: What cook uses, one eating popular Italian food

indicators.note: the first pieces swallow the second, which ends up inside them

parts.note: a cook fries or boils in a pan
I is the Roman numeral for one
in means fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: A chef's equipment and a diner tucking into a trendy Italian dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Panini are grilled Italian sandwiches, a familiar item of Italian food.

clue.text: Getting stick about high teas, having dressed down

indicators.note: the stick goes around the other letters, enclosing them

parts.note: a rod is a stick

indicators.note: high here means drunk or intoxicated, so the letters of teas are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone takes criticism over a lavish afternoon tea after being scolded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High tea' is a British early-evening meal, which disguises 'high' as part of the scene rather than the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To be roasted is to be harshly criticised, the same as being given a dressing-down.

clue.text: It's foul running water in North America

parts.note: yuk is an exclamation of disgust at something foul
a machine that is running is on

explanation.surface: A disgusting stream flows through the North American wilderness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'running water' looks like one phrase; 'running' is a separate piece.
explanation.definitionFit: The Yukon is a major river flowing through Canada and Alaska, so a body of water there.

clue.text: "It's stifling in Post Office", newspaperman snapped

indicators.note: the heat word sits inside the abbreviation for the post office

parts.note: stifling weather is hot
ED is short for editor, the newspaperman in charge

explanation.surface: A journalist complains about the heat in the post office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'snapped' seems to mean spoke sharply; it means took a picture.
explanation.definitionFit: To snap is to take a quick photograph, so snapped means photographed.

clue.text: What wine smuggler did to get rifle

parts.note: smugglers are said to run goods such as guns or liquor
sack is an old name for a dry Spanish white wine, like sherry

explanation.surface: A smuggler bringing in wine in order to buy a gun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rifle' looks like a gun; here it is a verb for searching and looting.
explanation.definitionFit: To ransack and to rifle both mean to search a place thoroughly and steal from it.

clue.text: Object in orbit letter's spoken of

indicators.note: spoken signals that the word is said aloud and a word with the same sound is meant

parts.note: the ninth letter of the alphabet, I

explanation.surface: A satellite is described as being shaped like a letter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'orbit' seems to mean space; it is the eye socket.
explanation.definitionFit: The orbit is the bony socket of the skull, and the thing lodged in it is the organ of sight.

clue.text: Time to stop women chatting up London's mayor

indicators.note: the time letter plugs a gap in the other words, as a stopper fills a hole

parts.note: hitting on someone is flirting with them, chatting them up
T is the abbreviation for time in physics

explanation.surface: A call for the capital's leader to stop flirting with women.
explanation.walkthrough: Dick Whittington was a medieval Lord Mayor of London, now a pantomime hero.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard Whittington served several times as Lord Mayor of London around 1400.

clue.text: Day younger goddess admits a rampant desire

parts.note: Sat is short for Saturday
yr is an abbreviation for younger

indicators.note: the goddess lets the letter in, so it goes inside her name

parts.note: Isis was an Egyptian goddess

explanation.surface: On some day a junior goddess confesses to wild lust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'admits' puts A inside ISIS to make IASIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Satyriasis is uncontrollable sexual craving in men, named after the lustful satyrs.

clue.text: Lack of principles said to obstruct friendship

indicators.note: the spoken word is put in the way, blocking the middle of the friendship

parts.note: amity is friendly relations, friendship
oral means spoken rather than written

explanation.surface: Unprincipled words are being said to get in the way of a friendship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'said' looks like a homophone signal, but it is a plain synonym for spoken.
explanation.definitionFit: Amorality is having no moral principles at all, being neither good nor wicked.

clue.text: Like poems close to Leonardo DiCaprio's heart

indicators.note: the letters sit close to the middle of the actor's name, inside it

explanation.surface: Poetic lines that touch the film star deeply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close to' says the run is near, not exactly at, the centre of the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Odic means relating to odes, so it describes a kind of poems.

clue.text: Cold cut of meat containing a seed from Cuba, say

indicators.note: the first pieces hold the letter a inside them

parts.note: C stands for cold on taps
a rib is a cut of meat
a bean is a seed

explanation.surface: A chilled meat dish with a seed in it, imported from Cuba.
explanation.walkthrough: 'containing' puts A inside C + RIB to make CARIB.
explanation.definitionFit: Cuba is an island in the Caribbean, so something from Cuba is an example of Caribbean origin.

clue.text: Top select group, one defending art, perhaps

definitions.text: Top select group, one defending art, perhaps

indicators.note: the outer letters surround and protect the scrambled word
to top something is to cut off its head, so the first letter goes

parts.note: the elite are a select group
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: perhaps says the letters of art may be in another order

explanation.surface: The cultured few stand up for the arts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top' is a verb, beheading the select group; the whole clue also describes the answer, as the literati champion art.
explanation.definitionFit: The literati are the educated, literary elite, a select group who champion culture.

clue.text: Over 501

parts.note: read 501 as Roman five hundred followed by the word for 1, and the result means over or finished; a darts game of 501 ends once completed

explanation.surface: A darts player's starting score, finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 501 splits as D, the Roman numeral for 500, plus ONE written as a word; 501 is also the starting score in darts.
explanation.definitionFit: Done means finished, as a game that is over.

clue.text: Russian writer knocked back very fine port

indicators.note: knocked back means the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: OK means fine
Oban is a port on the west coast of Scotland

explanation.surface: A Russian author downs an excellent port wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked back' suggests drinking the port; it reverses V + OK + OBAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Vladimir Nabokov was a Russian-born author best known for Lolita.

clue.text: Digit's good, dividing number reportedly better

indicators.note: reportedly means a word that sounds like the number is used

parts.note: four is a number

indicators.note: the good letter splits the other letters into two parts

parts.note: finer means better

explanation.surface: A finger is good for splitting numbers, the better to count.
explanation.walkthrough: 'better' looks like a gambler; it is the comparative of fine.
explanation.definitionFit: The index finger is one of the digits of the hand.

clue.text: Good question about old lady's wartime protection

indicators.note: the question goes around the mother, enclosing her

parts.note: to ask is to question
an old lady is slang for one's mother, ma, here with possessive s

explanation.surface: A good question about an elderly woman's wartime safety gear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old lady' is British slang for one's mother.
explanation.definitionFit: A gas mask protected civilians and soldiers against poison gas in wartime.

clue.text: Person parading topless, who might take a bow

indicators.note: topless means the first letter in a down answer is removed

parts.note: a marcher parades

explanation.surface: A topless person on parade, who might take a bow for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take a bow' seems to mean acknowledging applause; it means using a longbow.
explanation.definitionFit: An archer shoots with a bow, so is someone who takes one up.

clue.text: Bishop and pope occupying hotel rooms? One has a trek to town centre

definitions.text: One has a trek to town centre

indicators.note: the clergymen take up residence inside the rooms

parts.note: a suite is a set of rooms in a hotel
B is the chess notation for bishop
Urban is the name of eight popes

explanation.surface: Senior clergy staying in a hotel, one making a long walk into town.
explanation.walkthrough: Urban is a papal name, borne by eight popes.
explanation.definitionFit: A suburbanite lives on the outskirts and so must commute some way into the city centre.

clue.text: County's low quality food packaging area

indicators.note: the food wraps around the letter, enclosing it

parts.note: slop is unappetising, watery food

explanation.surface: A county known for wrapping its poor-quality food.
explanation.walkthrough: SALOP is an old name for Shropshire, an English county bordering Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Salop is the traditional abbreviation and former official name for the county of Shropshire.

clue.text: Northerner's brief stay at a hotel in Paris?

parts.note: one written briefly as a numeral, 1, read as the letter I

parts.words: stay at a hotel in Paris
parts.note: nuit is French for night, the unit of a hotel stay

explanation.surface: An Arctic traveller's short overnight stop in a Parisian hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: A French hotel booking for a short stay reads '1 nuit', one night; the 1 stands as I.
explanation.definitionFit: The Inuit are indigenous peoples of the Arctic, so people of the far north.

clue.text: Lazy individual shedding pounds and blubber

indicators.note: shedding means losing the letter for pounds

parts.note: a slob is a lazy, untidy person
L stands for pounds sterling, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A couch potato loses weight but keeps their fat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blubber' looks like fat; it is a verb meaning to cry.
explanation.definitionFit: To sob and to blubber both mean to weep noisily.

clue.text: Divine female has milkshakes

indicators.note: shakes means the letters are shaken up into a new order

explanation.surface: A goddess who drinks milkshakes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'milkshakes' hides the anagram signal: 'shakes' rearranges HAS + MILK.
explanation.definitionFit: Lakshmi is the Hindu goddess of wealth and good fortune.

clue.text: Pirouetting in the raw, a nudist in the dark

indicators.note: Pirouetting says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A naked dancer spinning around in darkness.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters spanning 'the raw, a nudist' read backwards give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in the dark about something is to be ignorant or uninformed of it.

clue.text: Poor Sky TV reception — right shambles!

indicators.note: a shambles is a mess, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A viewer complains that their satellite television signal is a mess.
explanation.walkthrough: Sky TV is a British satellite television service.
explanation.definitionFit: Poverty-stricken means extremely poor, lacking money.
